agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Rogers diffusion analysis, adopter-stage assessment, diffusion characteristics, accelerators/inhibitors, and context-sensitive timing implications

analytical_question: How far have the stated technology and application actions diffused, which factors matter here, and what bounded timing implication follows?
general_et_finding: The supplied broad AI survey indicates widespread reported AI use, but that measure is not penetration of LLM assistants for this exact task. Do not substitute agentic scaling figures for ordinary LLM drafting-assistant diffusion. General diffusion evidence is identical for the two reconstructed instructor cases; a precise Rogers category for either application is not established.
application_finding: Separate internal memorandum drafts and maintenance-report summaries from public event-announcement release. Drafting is reversible; public communications can mislead residents and maintenance summaries may omit important facts. Exact municipal application stage is not established. Relative advantage: potential administrative service capacity versus existing templates and staff workflows, not billable-hour revenue (inference, conditional accelerator). Compatibility: documented review, privacy and public accountability govern fit; technical systems and skills were not supplied (case facts and inference, conditional). Complexity: review ownership, sensitive-record handling and approval of public statements are the concrete dependencies; do not assume banking-like integration (inference, mixed). Trialability: de-identified internal draft comparisons are more reversible than public release (inference, accelerator). Observability: turnaround, factual omissions and reviewer burden could be tracked, while broader public benefit is not measured (inference, limited).
organization_specific_finding: For the conservative 300-person parks department, compatibility with documented review and public accountability is the pivotal factor. A departmental review lead and municipal peer network could act as change agents (inference); no such influence is empirically measured here. Municipal appropriations and service outcomes replace consulting-fee assumptions. The embedded evidence capsule is shared with Case A, but no Case A response or municipal peer dataset was supplied; I cannot borrow missing evidence from an isolated run.

evidence.claim: Reported agent scaling differs by revenue size (40% versus 22%).
evidence.source_or_reference: M26 McKinsey The state of AI in 2026 https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai
evidence.notes: Population: 1,719 survey respondents across roles, industries and organization sizes in 97 countries; GDP-weighted Denominator: 40%: respondents in organizations above USD 1 billion revenue; 22%: respondents in smaller organizations. Subgroup counts not verified; total n=1,719 is NOT either subgroup denominator. Scope: Agentic AI; cross-industry, not a freight-payment or municipal sample Limits: Self-report, selection and weighting limitations; revenue size is not employee count. Does not identify Rogers category or safety.

evidence.claim: 88% reported regular AI use in at least one business function; this is not agentic or application-specific penetration.
evidence.source_or_reference: M25 McKinsey The state of AI in 2025 https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai-2025
evidence.notes: Population: 1,993 respondents in 105 countries across organizational roles, sectors and sizes; GDP-weighted Denominator: Overall AI-use figure: survey respondents, total n=1,993; not all firms in an economy. Function-level agent exhibit: n=1,933, asked of function users then rebased to total sample. Scope: Overall organizational AI; agent questions are separate measures Limits: Self-report; not a census. Do not combine function-level, any-function, scaling and fully-scaled measures.

evidence.claim: Context and constraints supplied in this case; mechanisms described above are analytical inferences, not measured outcomes.
evidence.evidence_type: Hypothetical case facts and explicitly labeled inference
evidence.notes: No survey denominator or observed deployment result. These are not empirical adoption measurements.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Hype-sensitive claim: widespread overall AI use does not establish agentic or exact-application mainstream status.
The packet contains no comparable-peer application penetration denominator; absent evidence does not establish that actual diffusion is low.
Source sample units, observation dates and dependence must be preserved; published operational scaling is not a Rogers category.

These responses were authored with Codex assistance in the revision chat, with access to feedback and all cases. They are reviewed examples, not blind independent model trials or observed deployments.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence in the bounded interpretation of supplied sources; low confidence in exact application-stage assignment. Context mechanisms are inference and require local testing. No precise adopter percentage or category is justified.
value_opportunity_implication: Assess staff capacity and public-service quality under appropriations; no billable hours or consulting revenue mechanism applies.
risk_governance_implication: Separate internal drafts from publication; privacy protection and accountable review remain prerequisites, with jurisdiction-specific rules not established by this packet.
recommendation_management_implication: Conditional timing implication over three years: sequence any bounded internal learning after review/privacy procedures are established, retain human approval before public release, and monitor municipal evidence. Conservative posture changes timing, not the general diffusion finding or an assigned adopter category. This is not a final adoption decision.
change_monitoring_triggers: Review evidence quarterly and upon a relevant dated peer deployment or material change in controls/integration.
A new case triggers reassessment, not automatic mainstream classification. Require an applicable population denominator and production definition before changing a diffusion-stage claim.
Internal measured quality and reviewer burden inform timing, but cannot establish market penetration.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Request dated comparable-municipal deployments, adopting/eligible-department denominator, observation period, draft/publication boundaries, review procedures, error denominators and service-quality outcomes; missing shared case-specific evidence must be provided explicitly.
Specify sampling frame, geography, organization size and exact action authority; separate pilots from sustained production and provide failure-rate denominators.
Obtain internal baseline and readiness evidence before a management deployment decision.
